brief: September US CPI ran hot: headline rose 0.6% m/m from 0.4%, core rose 0.3% for a second straight month above the 0.2% consensus, and the annual rate hit 2.6% from 2.4%. Markets pushed October hike odds to about 47% from about 20%, and the two-year yield rose 11bp to 4.90%. UBS now expects hikes in December and March and raised its end-December 10-year forecast to 4.9% from 4.6%, still below the current 5.24% level. Strong growth (H1 GDP near 2.5%, Q3 near 3%), a resilient labor market and ISM at 54.5 let the Fed focus on inflation without raising recession risk, so UBS expects equities to absorb higher rates, helped by 28% forecast S&P EPS growth this quarter, roughly half from semiconductors. Markets price about 3.5 further hikes versus UBS's baseline of two. UBS expects only December and March, then a hold to late 2027. Germany is pushing EU safeguards on Chinese goods after a record trade surplus, but UBS still expects equity gains over six to 12 months. Singapore's MAS held policy steady, surprising markets, though UBS still expects USDSGD to fall to 1.25. ASML raised its 2026 revenue outlook and sees AI-driven demand extending into 2029 and 2030.
